parsed.explanation: The 1976 repeal removed one charge, not exposure: police still apply indecency articles 324, 329 and 350 (three months to two years' imprisonment, fines, deportation for non-citizens) against people suspected of cross-dressing, with a documented 2009 conviction for wearing an abaya and a 2011 venue raid. Entry screening is documented as presentation-based, with the Interior Minister stating suspected effeminate homosexuals are barred at airports; deportation is written into the indecency provisions. There is no anti-discrimination law, no hate-speech protection for LGBTQ people, courts refuse trans claims citing Sharia, and Article 330 routes the charged to forced medical testing. No remedy is documented, and a decade of excluded researchers leaves the evidence base thin. This is state-directed enforcement against presentation, short of the documented torture and capital pathways in the lowest anchors.

entry_documents.exposure: Interior Minister states suspected effeminate homosexuals are banned at airport checks; pending bills bar LGBTQ foreigners from entry/residency; indecency provisions carry deportation for non-citizens.
entry_documents.interaction: Presentation-based screening at the border can convert a document check into refusal, removal, or a fraud/indecency referral feeding detention.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Articles 324/329/350 carry three months to two years' imprisonment, fines and deportation, and have been used against cross-dressing and suspected LGBTQ people (2009 abaya sentence; 2011 raid). Article 330 mandates hospital STD testing after charge.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented; courts have refused trans claims citing Sharia.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A charge routes the visitor from police custody to a medical facility, compounding exposure and possible removal.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No LGBTQ shelters, facilities or registered organisations; association registration may be refused as contrary to morality; Article 330 medical detention.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Without any community or shelter infrastructure, a stranded visitor has no fallback and no one to vouch for them.

care_services.exposure: May 2023 court denied a trans man legal gender recognition and gender-affirming care, refusing a health-ministry examination; 2023 ruling held sex-reassignment contrary to Sharia absent intersex traits.
care_services.interaction: Clinical settings are also state reporting points, so seeking care can itself trigger disclosure and referral.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No protection from discrimination or hate speech; Article 309 protects religious groups only; false accusations of homosexuality used against critics; 2024 press caricature; further moral legislation adopted February 2024.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Police are the enforcement agent rather than a recourse, so threats and denunciations escalate rather than resolve.

minors_guardians.exposure: Education Ministry treats gender nonconformity as a disciplinary matter; school officials investigated and a manager dismissed in February 2024; pending bills instruct teachers to spot 'warning signs' and punish children.
minors_guardians.interaction: A gender-nonconforming minor travelling with a guardian has no documented protection and any institutional contact frames them as a problem.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence figure with a denominator is documented; hate speech against LGBTQ people carries no consequence; police enforcement targets presentation.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Reporting an assault means handing identity documents to the same officers documented as arresting for presentation.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination or hate-crime recourse; courts hostile; human-rights researchers excluded for a decade, leaving thin and partly remote sourcing; unresolved conflict over whether sodomy remains illegal.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: With no working remedy and a censored evidence base, residual unknowns resolve toward the documented enforcement pattern rather than toward safety.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra bars noncompliant trans visitors via an unpublished register, with exclusion and humiliation but no arrest or charge. This jurisdiction goes further: presentation-based airport screening sits on top of an indecency statute used to imprison and deport, so it rates below that anchor.

Varnalia detains, photographs and fines visitors in raids, with imprisonment rare, appeals slow but occasionally successful, and no deportation regime. Here imprisonment (up to two years) and deportation for non-citizens are written into the operative provisions and a cross-dressing conviction is documented, with no successful remedy recorded.

Varnalia's lowest tier features routine arrest at transit checks, months of pretrial custody, beatings and a latent capital clause. No custody abuse, prolonged pretrial detention or capital pathway for presentation is documented here, so it sits above that anchor.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is a formal decriminalisation that leaves enforcement intact. Repeal of the sodomy statute in 1976 removed one charge while articles 324, 329 and 350 supply a live arrest power applied to cross-dressing, with imprisonment and deportation for non-citizens; Article 330 adds forced medical testing after charge. The border is a documented exposure in its own right, with the Interior Minister describing presentation-based airport exclusion and pending bills to bar LGBTQ foreigners. Courts, ministries and the association registrar are aligned against recognition, there is no anti-discrimination or hate-crime recourse, and a decade of excluded researchers makes the record thin. Discovery is therefore likely to be followed by exclusion, charge or removal with no working remedy, but no documented torture or capital pathway places it above the lowest anchors.
